analysis: Examined units: docs/architecture/inference.md head 4923-5433 (unchanged context; the only doc change is head line 2126, which is not in these units). It describes stop-string scoping for Gemma 4/<think> reasoning spans via ReasoningStopScope. Also examined the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (7933a0f -> 7f00abc) and EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift head lines 15, 32, 64 and 159-160. In the bridge, the new optional stopStringScope parameter defaults to nil and is threaded to matchedStopSequence(scope:). It affects only usageSignal.record of the matched stop sequence, i.e. reported usage metadata. No change is visible to encryption (T-008), prefix-cache scope/salt (T-041), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), billing token counts or routing. The scope narrows which text spans are eligible for matching. The documentation claims the reported sequence replays the request's scope, which is consistent. A wrong scope could mis-report a stop match but would not leak plaintext: the reasoning-span exclusion keeps hidden reasoning out of match reporting rather than exposing it. Integration questions: (1) the submodule content is not visible. ReasoningStopScope, CBv2StopStringScope and the StopHoldback changes live there or in other files. Verify that holdback still withholds text before stop detection, so no reasoning/tool-call text or post-stop text streams to consumers. Also verify that a scope starting inside reasoning cannot cause hidden reasoning to be emitted. (2) Confirm the callers that pass stopStringScope (EngineV2Bridge submit paths, EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift) supply the same scope the engine used. (3) The submodule bump may include other mlx-swift-lm changes (KV/prefix, kernels) that this batch cannot see. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
